'''Ayyappanpillai Ajayaghosh''' (born 30 July 1962) is a research scientist/academician in the domain of interdisciplinary chemistry, and the former Director of the [[National Institute for Interdisciplinary Science and Technology]].<ref name="Director">{{Cite web |url=http://www.niist.res.in/english/director |title=Director |date=2016 |publisher=National Institute for Interdisciplinary Science and Technology}}</ref> He is known for his studies on [[supramolecular assemblies]], organogels, photoresponsive materials, chemosensory and security materials systems<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{Cite web |url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/Detail.aspx?AID=111 |title=Brief Profile of the Awardee |date=2016 |publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize |access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref> and is an elected fellow of all the three major Indian science academies viz. the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]],<ref name="NASI profile">{{Cite web|url=http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=A |title=NASI profile |date=2016 |publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130726040729/http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=A |archive-date=2013-07-26 }}</ref> [[Indian National Science Academy]]<ref name="The Year Book 2016">{{Cite web |url=http://www.insaindia.res.in/pdf/YearBook_2016.pdf |title=The Year Book 2016 |date=2016 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=8 January 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161104001952/http://www.insaindia.res.in/pdf/YearBook_2016.pdf |archive-date=4 November 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]]<ref name="Fellow profile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Ajayaghosh,_Dr_Ayyappanpillai |title=Fellow profile |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref> as well as [[The World Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="TWAS fellow">{{Cite web |url=https://twas.org/member/ajayaghosh-ayyappanpillai |title=TWAS fellow |date=2016 |publisher=The World Academy of Sciences}}</ref> The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the Government of India for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards for his contributions to Chemical Sciences in 2007.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx | title=View Bhatnagar Awardees | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref> He is the first chemist to receive the Infosys Science Prize for physical sciences, awarded by the Infosys Science Foundation. He received the [[TWAS Prize]] of [[The World Academy of Sciences]] in 2013 and the Goyal prize in 2019.<ref name="Ayyappanpillai Ajayaghosh – 2013 TWAS Prize Winner in Chemistry">{{Cite web |url=https://twas.org/ayyappanpillai-ajayaghosh-2013-twas-prize-winner-chemistry |title=Ayyappanpillai Ajayaghosh – 2013 TWAS Prize Winner in Chemistry |date=2016 |publisher=The World Academy of Sciences}}</ref>

== Biography ==
[[File:NIIST (2).jpg|left|thumb|235x235px|CSIR-NIIST]]
A. Ajayaghosh, born on 30 July 1962 in [[Kollam district|Kollam]] in the south Indian state of [[Kerala]], graduated in science from the [[University of Kerala]] and completed his master's degree from Calicut university in 1984. Subsequently, working under the guidance of Prof. [[V. N. Rajasekharan Pillai]], he secured a Ph.D. from [[University of Calicut]] in 1989; his thesis was on Solid-Phase Peptide Synthesis.<ref name="Faculty profile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.niist.res.in/english/about-dr-ayyappanpillai-ajayaghosh |title=Faculty profile |date=2016 |publisher=CSIR – National Institute for Interdisciplinary Science and Technology}}</ref>

His career started in 1988 at the Regional Research Laboratory, presently the [[National Institute for Interdisciplinary Science and Technology]] (NIIST), of the [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], as a Scientist and held various positions before promoting to an Outstanding  Scientist (Scientist-H)<ref name="Ayyappanpillai Ajayaghosh – CSIR">{{Cite web |url=http://followscience.com/content/538993/ayyappanpillai-ajayaghosh-csir-national-institute-for/ |title=Ayyappanpillai Ajayaghosh – CSIR |date=2016 |publisher=Follow Science}}</ref> and the head of the Photosciences and Photonics Group of NIIST. Subsequently he became the head of the Chemical Sciences and Technology group<ref name="Head, Photosciences and Photonics Group">{{Cite web |url=http://ip-science.thomsonreuters.com/ssr/researchday_09_in/ajayaghosh.html |title=Head, Photosciences and Photonics Group |date=2016 |publisher=Thomson Reuters}}</ref> He was the director of the Institute from 2015 and held the additional responsibility as the Dean of Chemical Sciences, [[Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research]] (AcSIR) New Delhi.<ref name="Director" /> In between, he was as an [[Alexander von Humboldt Fellow]] at the [[Max Planck Institute for Chemical Energy Conversion|Max Planck Institute for Strahlen Chemie]], Germany during 1994–96.<ref name="Awardee profile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.infosys-science-foundation.com/prize/laureates/2012/ajayaghosh.asp |title=Awardee profile |date=2016 |publisher=Infosys Science Foundation}}</ref> He served as an adjunct professor of Material Science Programme at the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur]].<ref name="Ayyappanpillai Ajayaghosh – CSIR" /> Presently, he is a J. C. Bose National Fellow at CSIR-NIIST and an adjunct professor at IISER Thiruvananthapuram.

Ajayaghosh is married to Ambili, and together they have two children, one of whom is Anantharaman Ajay, known for his roles in the 2023 movie "[[Romancham]]", [[Gaganachari]], and the [[YouTube]] channel "Appooppan and the Boys","Nissaram". The family resides in [[Thiruvananthapuram]], Kerala.<ref name="Ayyappanpillai Ajayaghosh – CSIR" />

== Legacy ==
Ajayaghosh's research have been principally in the fields of supramolecular chemistry, chemosensors, low band-gap polymers, fluorescent gels, organic nanostructures, and photoresponsive systems<ref name="New PCCP Associate Editor">{{Cite web |url=https://blogs.rsc.org/cp/2013/01/09/new-pccp-associate-editor-dr-ajayaghosh/ |title=New PCCP Associate Editor |date=2016 |publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry}}</ref> and he is reported to have done extensive researches on [[Supramolecular assembly|supramolecular architecture]] and light-induced sensor systems.<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee" /> He is known to have pioneered the study of molecular self-assembly in India and is credited with the creation of a new category of ''self-assembled materials that are functionally soft''.<ref name="Ayyappanpillai Ajayaghosh – 2013 TWAS Prize Winner in Chemistry" /> His work assisted in the design of larger molecular structures using self-assembling molecules and demonstrated ways to control their electrical conductivity through controlling external factors like temperature which have reported use in applications involving light harvesting, sensing, imaging, and security. He was the first scientist to design functional Phenylenevinylene-based [[Organogels]] from designed building blocks, which has been detailed in his article, ''First Phenylenevinylene Based Organogels:  Self-Assembled Nanostructures via Cooperative Hydrogen Bonding and π-Stacking'', published in 2001.<ref name="First Phenylenevinylene Based Organogels:  Self-Assembled Nanostructures via Cooperative Hydrogen Bonding and π-Stacking">{{Cite journal |last=A. Ajayaghosh, Subi J. George |title=First Phenylenevinylene Based Organogels: Self-Assembled Nanostructures via Cooperative Hydrogen Bonding and π-Stacking |journal=J. Am. Chem. Soc. |date=2001 |volume=123 |issue=21 |pages=5148–5149 |doi=10.1021/ja005933+|pmid=11457366 }}</ref> One of the commercial applications of his research is secret writing, ''thermally writable, non-copyable, and erasable fluorescent images useful for secret documentation by using a fluorescent gelator entrapped in a polystyrene film'' and the process has been developed by his team.<ref name="Secret letter writing gets a material boost">{{Cite journal |title=Secret letter writing gets material boost |journal = Nature India|date=4 January 2010 |doi=10.1038/nindia.2009.361 |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nindia.2009.361 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> His studies have been documented in several peer-reviewed articles;<ref name="Browse by Fellow">{{Cite web |url=https://repository.ias.ac.in/view/fellows/Ajayaghosh=3AAyyappanpillai=3A=3A.html |title=Browse by Fellow |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref> [[ResearchGate]] and [[Google Scholar]], online repositories of scientific articles, have listed 202<ref name="On ResearchGate">{{Cite web |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Jyotiranjan_Ray |title=On ResearchGate |date=2016 }}</ref> and 162 of them respectively.<ref name=" On Google Scholar">{{Cite web |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=bYdujAwAAAAJ&hl=en |title=On Google Scholar |date=2016 |publisher=Google Scholar}}</ref> He also holds patents for several processes he has developed.<ref name="Patents by Inventor Ayyappanpillai Ajayaghosh">{{Cite web |url=http://patents.justia.com/inventor/ayyappanpillai-ajayaghosh |title=Patents by Inventor Ayyappanpillai Ajayaghosh |date=2016 |publisher=Justia Patents}}</ref>

Ajayaghosh is associated with several science journals around the world. He is an associate editor of [[Physical Chemistry Chemical Physics]] (PCCP), published by the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]]<ref name="New PCCP Associate Editor" /> and a senior editor of the [[Bulletin of the Chemical Society of Japan]].<ref name="About BCSJ">{{Cite web |url=http://www.journal.csj.jp/bcsj/about |title=About BCSJ |date=2016 |publisher=CSJ Journals}}</ref> He is a former member of the advisory board of [[RSC Advances]] and sits in the editorial board of ''Chemistry: An Asian Journal''.<ref name=" Editorial Board CAAJ">{{Cite web |url=http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/journal/10.1002/(ISSN)1861-471X/homepage/2451_edbd.html |title=Editorial Board CAAJ |date=2016 |publisher=Chemistry: An Asian Journal|doi=10.1002/(ISSN)1861-471X }}</ref> He has also guided several master's and doctoral scholars in their studies and has been involved in programs for the popularization of science and science awareness campaigns.<ref name="Faculty profile" />
